t: Metellus and Pompey concentrate operations against Celtiberians
c: In 74 BC, Caecilius Metellus and Pompey concentrated their operations against the Celtiberians and Vaccaei.

c: In 49 BC, Julius Caesar invaded Italy, effectively declaring war on the Roman Senate.

t: Battle of Munda between Caesar and Pompeius
c: The final battle was between Caesar and Gnaeus Pompeius, the son of Pompey, supported by Titus Labienus and Publius Attius Varus, in 45 BC.

t: Cantabrian Wars begin against northern tribes
c: The Cantabrian Wars were fought between the Romans and the Gallaeci, Cantabrians and Astures of northern Hispania.

t: Augustus takes personal command of campaigns
c: Augustus took the command in 26 BC, the fourth year of the war.

t: Augustus reaches Tarraco in eastern Hispania
c: He reached Tarraco (Tarragona) in eastern Hispania in 27 BC, but he arrived in the area too late for fighting before winter set in.

t: Titus Statilius Taurus commands Cantabrian campaigns
c: In 29 BC, the Roman commander was Titus Statilius Taurus.

t: Sextus Appuleius conducts campaigns in Hispania
c: In 28 and 27 BC it was Sextus Appuleius, who celebrated a triumph in 26 BC.

t: War fought against the Astures
c: In 25 BC the war was fought only against the Astures.

c: After the death of emperor Majorian in 461 Roman authority collapsed except in Tarraconensis the northeastern quadrant of the peninsula.

c: The Visigoths, a Germanic people, whose kingdom was located in southwest Gaul, took the province when they occupied Tarragona in 472.

c: In 484 the Visigoths established Toledo as the capital of their kingdom.

c: In 585 the Visigoths conquered the Suebic Kingdom of Galicia, and thus controlled almost all of Hispania.

c: It was taken by the Roman general Scipio Africanus in the year 209 BC during the Second Punic War to cut off the silver going to general Hannibal.

c: In the year 44 BC, the city received the title of colony under the name Colonia Urbs Iulia Nova Carthago (CVINC), founded by citizens of Roman law.

c: 721 – An Umayyad army led by Al-Samh crushed by duke Odo's Aquitanian army at the Battle of Toulouse ("Balat Al Shuhada" of Toulouse).

c: Ceuta (which was briefly recaptured by the Visigoths in 540) became a part of Mauretania.
